full_judgment:
Pre opposite parties filed Misc. Case No. 70 of 1979 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Chandpur under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, contending inter alia that the pre-emptor was the sharer in the disputed holding along with opposite party Nos. 2-4 Pre-emptee petitioners are not the co-sharer of the disputed holding. Pre-emptee petitioners purchased 30 decimals of land from seller opposite party No. 2 to 4 by registered sale deed dated 2.8.76 for a consideration of Tk. 2000/-. No notice of the sale was served upon the pre opposite party as per provision of law. Subsequently pre-emptor opposite party came to know of the alleged sale from Md. Fazar Ali on 8th Chaitra, 1385 B. S. and thereafter obtained certified copy of the sale deed from Hajiganj S.R. Office and became fully aware of the sale on 1.4.79. Pre-emptor opposite parry made the deposit with compensation and filed the case seeking pre-emtion of the disputed transfer. 

 7. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner that the learned Subordinate Judge committed error of law occasioning failure of justice in affirming the judgment and order passed by the learned Assistant Judge holding that although the petitioners are co-shares in the disputed holding by gift prior to the transfer sought to be pre-empted, their status are not better than that of a co-sharer which is contrary to the provision contained in sub-Section 10, clause "A" of section96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 8. In order to expose the misconception of law, the learned Advocate appearing for the pre-emptee petitioner has relied on sub- section 10 clause 'A' of Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which reads thus: 

 "10 Nothing in this section shall apply to (a) a transfer to a co-sharer in the tenancy whose interest has accrued otherwise than by purchase; or" 

 10. Both the courts below misinterpreted the provision of Sub-section clause 'A' of Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The transfer sought to be pre-empted is view of the cited decision referred above. The cited decision relates to the transferred made under section 26F of the Bengal Tenancy Act but the principle laid down therein is folly applicable to the instant case inasmuch as East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is said to the successor of Bengal Tenancy Act such provides for pre-emption under section 96 of the Act. Exception- has been made by subsection 10 of Section 96 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act with respect to certain transfer by excepting them from operation of pre emption and clause 'A' of sub-section 96 Of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act exempts transfer to co-sharer of the tenancy whose interest has accrued otherwise than by purchase from pre-emption. This provision is similar to the provision of Section 26(FX1) (a) of Bengal Tenancy Act. It is, therefore, obvious that co-sharer in the tenancy whose existing interest has accrued otherwise than by purchase i.e. by way of gift as in the present case is protected from pre-emption. 

 11. Both the Courts below put a wider meaning on the word "purchase". Thus the policy of law which exempts a co-sharer whose existing interest has accrued otherwise than purchase from pre-emption. The word "purchase" occurring in sub-section 10 clause ('a') of Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act should not be stretched so much in order to include transfer by way of gift in the category of transfer by purchase. 

 12. Thus, having considered the entire materials on record and facts involved in the instant case, I am of opinion 'that both the Courts committed error in law in interpreting the provision contained in sub-section 10 of clause 'A' of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and as such the judgment and order a not sustainable in law.
